Precision matrix for Whittle-Matérn fields

Source: R/spde_precision.R
spde_precision.Rd

Computes a sparse precision matrix for a Whittle-Matérn field. Order three returns an unconstrained edge-endpoint precision. Fractional orders return the unconstrained joint precision of the rational-approximation components.

Usage

spde_precision(
  kappa,
  tau,
  alpha,
  graph,
  BC = 1,
  build = TRUE,
  m = 2,
  type_rational_approx = "chebfun",
  type_interp = "spline"
)

Arguments

kappa

Positive range parameter; zero is also supported for alpha 1.

tau

Positive precision parameter.

alpha

Smoothness parameter, strictly greater than 0.5 and at most 3.

graph

A metric_graph object.

BC

Boundary-condition code, one of 0, 1, 2, or 3, passed unchanged to the alpha-one and alpha-two backends. BC = 1 adds stationary endpoint corrections; BC = 0 adds no additional corrections. Codes 2 and 3 retain their backend-specific interpretation. Ignored for alpha 3 and fractional alpha: these return boundaryless raw precisions, with constraints imposed separately.

build

If TRUE, the precision matrix is returned. Otherwise a list with entries i, j, x, and dims is returned. As for the integer cases, build = FALSE is not supported for graph_components objects.

m

Rational approximation order for fractional alpha. A positive integer; ignored for alpha 1, 2, and 3. Defaults to 2.

type_rational_approx

Rational approximation type passed to rSPDE; one of "chebfun", "brasil", and "chebfunLB". Used only for fractional alpha. Defaults to "chebfun".

type_interp

Coefficient interpolation method passed to rSPDE; one of "linear", "log", "spline", and "logspline". Used only for fractional alpha. Defaults to "spline".

Value

Precision matrix or triplet list. The existing alpha-one and alpha-two representations are unchanged.

Details

For fractional alpha, the component order is Q0, Q1, ..., Qm. The zeroth component has graph$nV vertex coordinates when alpha is below one, and 2 * floor(alpha) * graph$nE endpoint coordinates otherwise. Each remaining component has 2 * ceiling(alpha) * graph$nE coordinates. Endpoint coordinates follow edge order, with the process and its successive derivatives at the start followed by those at the end of each edge. Parameter scaling and the boundaryless edge correction are included, but no constraint basis or observation map is applied. For alpha 3, the result is a single 6 * graph$nE square raw matrix, ordered as process value, first derivative, and second derivative at each edge start and then end. No rational approximation is used for alpha 3. The returned raw matrix need not be positive definite before the graph constraints are imposed. Neither observations nor graph$PtV are required, and C, CoB, and the constraint cache are left unchanged. For graph_components, entire joint matrices are assembled in component order, as in the integer cases.
